title: What is Abiogenesis?
intro: A Partner at a VC firm I look up to told me that to start a career in Venture Capital, it’s important to either:
list: And/or have an opinion/ set of core beliefs about certain topics.
body: Abiogenesis is a culmination of that thought. It’s where I’ve decided to document whatever I do on that front. It’s a space where I dump all the information I find about the topics that I’m passionate about, a place where I can come back to see it in a structured manner. I’m also tracking certain startups that I think are interesting and following them on their journey. I’m basically just reading up, trying to form an opinion, and then making wild guesses about the future—just like VCs do now, and hopefully, like I will one day.
Abiogenesis also acts as accountability and motivation and a good reminder of where I started and where I am right now. Long way to go, but I’m excited.

sections.title: Why is this called Abiogenesis?
body: The concept of abiogenesis discusses the origin of life from non-living matter. What was once a philosophical curiosity is now a scientific pursuit with profound implications for modern industries. I like this principle of creating from nothing, of generating self-sustaining value where none existed before. That’s the heart of venture capital.

Urey and Miller postulated that the right environmental conditions and catalytic forces allowed simple molecules to evolve into complex compounds and eventually life. I imagine Venture Capital as that catalytic force that turns ideas or mere concepts into thriving, living organizations. Early-stage startups are fragile and require the right conditions and support to survive.

In the economic primordial soup, ideas float as free molecules. They have the potential but need structure. VC acts as the energy source that binds ideas together, evolving them. The fittest survive and gain momentum, iterating through survival, securing market share, and being the dominant species in the business ecosystem.
Venture Capital is abiogenesis in action, where nothing, in the right case, can become everything.
